rendering.persona_description: Aleksander is a 52-year-old pharmacist who has run the same independent pharmacy for almost twenty years. He's married to Dana, his wife of fourteen years, and describes himself as someone who likes things settled and doesn't enjoy surprises. He reads a lot of nonfiction, keeps a tidy garage, and is well liked by regular customers who say he remembers their prescriptions without looking them up.
rendering.clinical_context: Aleksander has no mental-health presentation. Like most people, he occasionally has a passing thought wondering whether he truly loves Dana or married the right person; these thoughts crop up now and then, particularly since his father-in-law died and old memories of early disagreements in the marriage came back to him. The thoughts pass on their own within minutes, and he doesn't do anything to try to resolve or get rid of them.
rendering.behavioral_description: Aleksander will mention, in an easygoing way, that he sometimes wonders whether he really loves Dana, especially when he's tired or after a disagreement, but he treats it as an ordinary passing thought rather than something worth dwelling on. He doesn't bring it up repeatedly or look to others to reassure him about it; if the subject comes up, he shrugs it off and moves on to whatever he actually wants to talk about, whether that's the pharmacy, a book he's reading, or weekend plans.
